rows.name: Declarative environment config file
rows.offer: A checked-in devcontainer.json describes how the development container is built, configured and connected to.

flisk.reason: Flisk's checked-in file is a service.json per service; it describes the running services, not the developer toolchain.

rows.name: Toolchain from image or Dockerfile
rows.offer: The dev container is created from a registry image or a Dockerfile so every developer gets the same installed tools and versions.

flisk.reason: Installing the developer toolchain is a decision left to Dev Containers or Devbox; Flisk only checks tools with flisk doctor and runs the services (docs/compare/dev-environments.md).

rows.name: Features: shareable install units
rows.offer: Features are packaged install scripts plus config that add a tool or runtime to any dev container by referencing an id.

flisk.reason: Toolchain installation is out of scope by design; Flisk's own resource features (nats, prisma, redis) configure services, not developer machines.

rows.name: Templates to start a project
rows.offer: Pick a starting Template from a filterable index and the tool writes the dev container configuration files for you.

flisk.reason: Flisk scaffolds services and whole starter stacks rather than editor container configs.

rows.name: Several named configurations per repo
rows.offer: A repository can hold more than one devcontainer.json in sub-folders and the user picks which environment to open.

flisk.reason: Flisk selects among named stacks with flisk up [stack].

rows.name: Generate a .devcontainer config
rows.offer: A command writes a ready dev container configuration into the project so any supporting editor or cloud host can open it.

flisk.reason: Flisk already detects devcontainer and Codespaces hosts and its starter has Codespaces/DevPod buttons, so scaffolding a config that installs flisk and reaches Docker fits the one-command story.

rows.acceptance: flisk project writes .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (flisk install, Docker access, forwarded gateway port) and a test in cli/src/commands/__tests__ plus a docs/agent-hosts.md text proves it.

ice.basis: Impact 6: Codespaces/DevPod users are a named launch path; confidence 6: the page documents the generator but not what users ask for; ease 5: cli/src/commands/project.ts already scaffolds files, but the container needs Docker access that must be designed.

rows.name: Shell inside a running service
rows.offer: Any terminal opened in the tool runs inside the container, so developers work with the same tools and runtime as the app.

flisk.reason: There is no flisk exec or shell for a service container or local-process service today, only logs and restart, and a one-command shell fits the debug loop for agents and people.

rows.acceptance: A flisk exec <resource> command (or MCP tool) is in cli/src/commands and the command tree, with a test; evidence would be {command: 'flisk exec'}.

ice.basis: Impact 5: debugging inside a service is common but docker exec works today; confidence 5: the source describes an editor terminal, so the CLI analogue is inferred; ease 5: cli/src/commands/logs.ts shows how to resolve a resource to a container, but local-process services have no container.

rows.name: Attach editor to running container
rows.offer: The editor can connect to an already running Docker container and remember per-image settings, extensions and folders.

flisk.reason: Editor integration is out of scope by design; Flisk works with any editor and leaves attaching to the editor's own Docker tooling.

rows.name: Editor extensions installed in container
rows.offer: Extension ids listed under customizations.vscode are installed inside the container when it is created.

flisk.reason: IDE integration is out of scope by design; Flisk does not ship an editor extension.

rows.name: Dotfiles applied to containers
rows.offer: The extension clones a personal dotfiles repository into every dev container so shell setup follows the developer.

flisk.reason: Personal shell setup belongs to the developer's editor or toolchain layer, not to a service runtime.

rows.name: Multi-container via Docker Compose
rows.offer: A dev container can reference Compose files and pick which services to start, instead of defining its own orchestrator.

flisk.reason: Flisk generates the Compose and Tilt files itself from service.json, with one gateway in front.

rows.name: Lifecycle commands on create and start
rows.offer: Hooks such as onCreateCommand, postCreateCommand and postStartCommand run setup scripts at defined moments of the container's life.

flisk.reason: Flisk orders one-shot setup with migrator resources and dependsOn, but has no generic per-service on-create or post-start hook.

rows.name: Port forwarding with attributes
rows.offer: Ports are forwarded to the host with labels and a choice to notify, open the browser or stay silent when a port appears.

flisk.reason: Flisk gives each service one gateway URL and flisk open launches it; there are no per-port label or auto-open options.

rows.name: Create and run without an editor
rows.offer: A reference command-line tool builds, starts and configures the dev container from devcontainer.json with no editor involved.
match: create and configure a dev container

rows.name: Reuse the same environment in CI
rows.offer: A GitHub Action and an Azure DevOps task run the repository's dev container in CI so local and CI builds match.

flisk.reason: Flisk documents a copy-paste GitHub Actions workflow, not a maintained Action or Azure DevOps task.

rows.name: Prebuilt environment images
rows.offer: The environment image is built once in CI, pushed to a registry with its configuration in a label, and reused so startup is fast.

flisk.reason: Flisk layers golden base images for faster local builds but does not publish a shared prebuilt team image.

rows.name: Rebuild after config change
rows.offer: A rebuild command re-creates the container so changes to the configuration take effect.

flisk.reason: Flisk live-updates containers while you code and restarts or regenerates when configuration changes.

rows.name: Docker access from inside the container
rows.offer: Features and the privileged and mounts properties let the dev container use Docker itself, for example docker-in-docker.

flisk.reason: Flisk detects whether a container runtime is reachable from a devcontainer or Codespace but does not configure that access.

rows.name: Containers on a remote host
rows.offer: The extension can run containers on a remote Docker host reached over SSH or a tunnel while the editor stays local.

flisk.reason: Remote editor sessions are editor integration and out of scope; Flisk is a local runtime on the machine with the repository.

rows.name: Hosted Codespaces and cloud hosts
rows.offer: The spec is supported by hosted services such as GitHub Codespaces and CodeSandbox that run the dev container in the cloud.

flisk.reason: Hosted cloud workspaces are out of scope by design; Flisk only detects when it is running inside one (flisk doctor).

rows.name: Declared minimum CPU and memory
rows.offer: hostRequirements states minimum CPUs, memory, storage and GPU so tools warn or pick a bigger machine.

flisk.reason: A stack of many containers can silently starve a small Docker VM, so a declared minimum that flisk doctor checks fits Flisk's diagnostics role.

rows.acceptance: service.json or the project config accepts a minimum memory/CPU and flisk doctor reports a pass or fail; evidence would be a text check in docs/service-json.md and a doctor test.

ice.basis: Impact 4: it helps people on small Docker VMs but is not an asked-for launch feature; confidence 5: the spec is clear but the Docker VM memory source differs by platform; ease 5: cli/src/commands/doctor.ts already holds many checks, though no host-memory check exists yet.

rows.name: Capabilities and security options
rows.offer: capAdd, securityOpt, privileged and init let a dev container add debugger capabilities such as SYS_PTRACE in a cross-orchestrator way.

flisk.reason: Debugging Go, Rust or C++ services inside containers needs ptrace, and a service.json passthrough would keep users from hand-editing generated Compose files, which AGENTS.md forbids.

rows.acceptance: service.json documents capAdd/securityOpt fields in docs/service-json.md, the Compose generator emits them, and flisk config verify passes; evidence would be a text check on that doc.

ice.basis: Impact 4: only debugger-in-container users need it; confidence 5: the spec property is clear, whether Flisk already passes it through was not found in docs; ease 4: touches the Starlark Compose generator and the schema in runtime/engine.

rows.name: Environment values from the host
rows.offer: containerEnv and remoteEnv set variables and can read the host environment with localEnv substitution.

text.contains: Nothing secret is ever written to a generated file.

rows.name: Docs written for coding agents
rows.offer: The VS Code docs point agents at an llms.txt and serve every article as Markdown by adding .md to its URL.
